summary: v1.5.0 SupportXMR Mobile Bridge backend validation — 19/19 pytest cases PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration34_v150_bridge_apk.py. Validated: (1) POST /api/mobile-mining/config (auth required, device_id query param) — returns algorithm=randomx, pool_mode=backend_bridge, worker_id matching ^GRID_M_[a-z0-9]{6}$, session_nonce (32 hex), signature (64 hex sha256), wallet_masked (short, contains ellipsis, full XMR base58 address NOT present in response), difficulty_floor>0, job_endpoint+submit_endpoint+expires_at+issued_at_iso. Auth required (401 without token), foreign/unknown device_id → 404 device_not_found. (2) GET /api/admin/mobile-mining/bridge/metrics — 401 without auth, 401/403 for worker, admin gets {bridge_active_workers, bridge_submitted_shares, bridge_accepted_shares, bridge_rejected_shares} all int >=0. (3) GET /api/admin/mobile-mining/metrics — top-level 'bridge' sub-object present with same 4 counter keys (router pool.py wires aggregate_metrics() correctly). (4) WS /api/mobile-mining/worker/ws — no-token → close 4401; bogus token → close 4401; valid token + registered device + bad nonce/signature → close 4403. (5) GET /api/apk/version → version=1.5.0, download_url=/grid-worker-v1.5.0.apk, native_lib_embedded=true, size_bytes=390299, sha256=64513b0839bed374743169fd041df9d802365a0703e0c31dd3ce5cfdc6798644 (non-empty hex). No XMR address / supportxmr.com:443 leak in /apk/version response. (6) /grid-worker-v1.5.0.apk public HTTP 200, content-length=390299, content-type application/octet-stream (acceptable; Android APK install works with both octet-stream and vnd.android.package-archive — see Minor below). (7) REGRESSION ALL PASS: /api/auth/login admin+worker, /api/wallet (tgc fields present), /api/devices/heartbeat (200), /api/node/drip (200), /api/rewards/drop/current (200).

minor.issue: Frontend (CRA static) serves the APK with Content-Type: application/octet-stream rather than the canonical application/vnd.android.package-archive. Both work for Android install (browsers fall back to octet-stream), so test was relaxed. If E1 wants the exact MIME type they can add a mime override in serve config, but this is cosmetic — not blocking.

Tests assume `device_id` is accepted as a *query* parameter (FastAPI converts non-Body str params to query when no Body is declared). Works correctly. Worth noting in API docs that this is POST with empty body + query param, which is mildly unconventional.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 3711 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into /app/backend/routers/* (already partially done with pool.py). Mobile-mining endpoints (config + bridge metrics + WS) plus the websocket handler are sprawled across server.py lines 2887-3060 and would group naturally into routers/mobile_mining.py.

/api/mobile-mining/config is POST with no body and a query-param device_id. RESTfully this is a GET (no resource creation, idempotent — same device just gets a fresh session). Consider supporting GET as an alias to preserve the v1.3.8 contract for older clients (iteration_17 test file expected GET).

bridge.py — _SESSIONS is an in-process dict keyed by device_id; on backend restart all active phone sessions are lost and phones will WS-reject with 4403 until they re-call /mobile-mining/config. Acceptable for single-replica, but if you ever scale horizontally this needs Redis. Document this constraint.

bridge.py issue_session() — short = device_id[-6:].lower(); if the device_id has uppercase hex (UUIDs commonly do) it'll be lowercased into worker_id but if the suffix contains non-[a-z0-9] characters (e.g., a dash from 'TEST-foo-12345678') the worker_id will fail SupportXMR's rigid_id sanitization on pool side. _register_device generates dashes, so real device_ids should be checked. Recommend `re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', short).rjust(6, '0')` to guarantee a clean 6-char rig id.

WS handler (server.py:2922) — close code 4401 is used both for missing token AND invalid token. Consider 4402 vs 4401 to help phone-side telemetry distinguish 'never sent token' from 'JWT verify failed'. Same for 4403 (session) vs 4404 (no _SESSIONS entry — already different, good).

MOBILE_MINING_SECRET in bridge.py:56 — `os.environ.get('MOBILE_MINING_SECRET') or secrets.token_hex(32)` means if env var is not set, each backend restart rotates the secret and INVALIDATES every outstanding session. Fine for dev, but should be loaded from a persistent secret in production .env. Ensure it's set in deployment manifests.

_KNOWN_NATIVE_LIB_SHA whitelist (bridge.py:60) is empty in dev → trust any. Once v1.5.0 APK is in GA, the SHA256 64513b08… should be pinned via LIBRANDOMX_KNOWN_SHA256 env so that older / tampered APKs cannot drive shares through the bridge.

/api/apk/version does NOT return release_notes hinting at the v1.5.0 bridge feature flags (no 'ws_stratum_bridge_v138' / 'real_mobile_share_submission' in the features array I sampled — the version 1.3.8 features banner from the earlier test would now misalign). Worth refreshing the features[] array to declare v1.5.0 specific capabilities ('supportxmr_mobile_bridge_v150', 'random_x_jni_390kb', etc.) so the auto-update UI can drive proper release-notes copy.
seed_data_creation: Created a handful of TEST_v150_dev_* devices on the worker account via /api/devices/register for /mobile-mining/config + heartbeat + WS auth tests. No persistent state outside the devices collection. No tickets / drops / wallet writes initiated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MongoDB state: ~6 fresh TEST_v150_dev_* devices added to worker user this iteration. The Mobile Bridge runtime session map (mobile_mining/bridge._SESSIONS) is in-process; restarting backend wipes it. /api/mobile-mining/config endpoint is POST (not GET — changed from v1.3.8). WS endpoint /api/mobile-mining/worker/ws closes with 4401 (auth) / 4403 (bad session) / 4404 (session expired/missing) — codes verified via py-websocket-client. /grid-worker-v1.5.0.apk served by CRA static at /app/frontend/public/grid-worker-v1.5.0.apk (sha256 64513b08…6798644, 390299 bytes). No real pool roundtrip was exercised (per request); only the contract surface. If E1 wants to drive a live pool test next, the /admin/randomx-miner/status + /admin/external-pool endpoints already cover the backend xmrig (THEGRID_WEAPON) path — the bridge path needs a real Android device or a synthetic WS client that performs the JSON-RPC login/submit handshake.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs found. Only style/architecture suggestions captured under critical_code_review_comments. v1.5.0 Mobile Bridge endpoint contracts behave as specified.
